misconception_description: Student believes that the body of an if-statement executes repeatedly as long as the condition holds.

solutions.generated_code:
program JumlahHarmonik
kamus
  n, i : integer
  jumlah : real
algoritma
  input(n)
  jumlah <- 0
  i <- 1
  if i <= n then
    jumlah <- jumlah + 1 / i
    i <- i + 1
  endif
  output(jumlah)
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student has replaced the recursive solution with an if-statement, genuinely believing it will execute repeatedly like a while loop. From their perspective, the if-statement will continuously check the condition (n >= 1), and as long as it's true, keep adding 1/n to result and decrementing n. They expect this to accumulate all terms of the harmonic sum from 1/n down to 1/1. In reality, the if-statement executes only once (or not at all), so the function returns either 1/n if n >= 1, or 0 if n < 1, instead of the full harmonic sum. This is a logical error stemming from confusing if-statements with while loops.
